lines.text: Keep clear of the falls. Lifeboats don't launch for empty pockets.
lines.journalNote: Bosun Hari guards the starboard davits like a warden. Thick rope and knotted muscle.

lines.text: The barometer's in the basement. Something ugly is coming up through the floorboards.
lines.journalNote: Hari senses the impending mutiny. He checks his cleaver and tightens the lifeboat winch.

lines.text: Kedar runs the deck now. I don't care whose head is on the sovereign, so long as it weighs true.
lines.journalNote: Hari switched allegiance to Kedar without blinking. Coin is his only creed.

lines.text: The cutter's our only chance! The winch is locked—you hold the release plate, I'll grease the gears!
lines.journalNote: Hari panics as the ship shudders. He yells that the winch plate will drop the lifeboat.

lines.text: One gold coin from the captain's stash. Bring me that, and this cutter drops into the swell with you in it.
lines.journalNote: Hari named his price: one gold coin from the captain's chest to launch the escape cutter.

lines.text: Saw something shining near the capstan. Silver locket. Left it alone. Dead men's trinkets bring bad water.
lines.journalNote: Hari saw a silver locket dropped near the capstan. Refused to touch it for fear of ill luck.

lines.text: Quartermaster. Your keys can open any locker, but only cold silver unlocks these lifeboat davits. Remember who holds the falls.
lines.journalNote: Hari eyed my belt with greedy respect. Coin is the only language he listens to.

lines.text: Charts won't float when the timbers crack, Navigator. Point us toward dry land, or we'll all be feeding the bottom.
lines.journalNote: Hari grumbled at the Navigator, anxious for charts that lead to solid ground.

lines.text: Move along, deckhand. Lifeboats are for men who pull their weight. You go over the side with the rats.
lines.journalNote: Hari shoved me aside. He treats deckhands as expendable ballast.

lines.text: Keep quiet and look to your own business. The wind is shifting, and words can get a throat cut.
lines.journalNote: Hari warns me that the tension on deck is ready to boil over.

lines.text: You heard that bird on the spar too, eh? Three cries means nobody gets an easy night on the Jal-Doot.
lines.journalNote: Hari recognized the three cries of the gull as an omen of ill fortune.
